title: Chapter 15: Boss Level 3: The Expense Tracker
video_title: Python Chapter 15: Boss Level 3, The Expense Tracker
summary: At closing time, nobody at the Corner Cafe knows where the money went. Follow Asha as she plans, builds and tests an expense tracker with a list of tuples, a set of categories, checked amounts and a dictionary of totals. She uses an AI assistant at all six stages. Tests catch three confident AI mistakes: a model that loses data, max() on a dictionary, and a shorter line that crashes.

messages.text: I am a beginner. I know lists, dictionaries, tuples and sets. I want to record the cafe's expenses: a category and an amount for each one. Do not write the program. Suggest how to store the expenses, and give one reason.

Store them in a dictionary. The category is the key and the amount is the value, for example `expenses["milk"] = 12.50`.
Then the totals are already there.

segments.say: In this project, all six AI stages help build one tracker, piece by piece. Stage 1: plan. Asha asks the AI how to store the expenses. No code yet.

scenes.title: Step 3: Check an amount
scenes.direction: Teach why isdigit fails for 12.50, the third value of replace, then ask which texts pass. A quiz, then a breather.

segments.say: Step 3: the amount. In Chapter 10, is digit checked a whole number. But 12.50 has a decimal point, and is digit says False for it.
The fix: remove one decimal point first, then check. Replace takes an optional third value: how many changes to make. Line 2 removes one point, so 12.50 becomes 1250.
Line 3 removes only the first point of 1.2.3, so it becomes 12.3. That still has a point.
Line 4 loops over six texts, and line 5 prints each one with the result of the check.

ask.question: Which of the six texts on line 4 print `True`?

after.say: Only two: 12.50 and 30. A comma, a word, a second point and a minus sign all fail.
Only text with at most one point and nothing but digits passes. Then float is safe.

visual.question: Which answer passes the amount check?
visual.explain: `0.75` loses its one point and becomes `075`: all digits. `1..5` keeps a second point.

segments.say: Quick check, with four new answers. Which one passes the amount check?

after.say: C, 0.75. Without its one point, it is 0 7 5: all digits. And 1, dot, dot, 5 keeps a second point, so it fails.

visual.heading: Generate: one line for the biggest

messages.text: My dictionary totals holds a total for each category. Write one line that finds the category with the biggest total. Tell me what it gives.

Here is the line: `biggest = max(totals)`
It gives the category that cost the most.

segments.say: Step 6: the biggest category. Stage 3: generate. Asha asks the AI for one line, and asks what it gives.
The AI writes biggest equals max of totals. It says this gives the category that cost the most. In Chapter 11, max found the largest number in a list, so it looks right.
But remember what a loop over a dictionary gives you, from Chapter 12.

ask.question: The AI says `max(totals)` gives the category that cost the most. Is it right?

after.say: No. Max goes through a dictionary like a loop does, so it compares the keys, not the totals. Asha tests it.

segments.say: Beans cost 30, the most. But the line prints milk!

visual.heading: Debug: the cause before the fix

messages.text: On a day with no expenses, my program stopped. Here are my lines and the full error. Explain the cause first. Then show a fix that works for every day.

An empty dictionary has no keys, so `max()` has nothing to choose from. And `max()` compares the keys, not the totals.
The fix: start `biggest` at "none" and keep the biggest category so far in a loop.

segments.say: Stage 5: debug. Asha pastes her lines and the full error report. She asks for the cause first.
The AI explains: an empty dictionary has no keys, so max has nothing to choose from. And it agrees that max compares the keys.
Its fix: start biggest at the text none, and keep the biggest category so far in a loop.

Here are the results: beans, cups, repairs, and none for the empty day. All four days pass!

visual.heading: Recap
visual.label: What you used
items: Keep each record as a tuple in a list, so nothing is lost.
Build totals with `get(key, 0)`. A set of allowed values rejects anything else.
`replace(".", "", 1)` and `isdigit()` check an amount before `float()`.
`max()` on a dictionary compares the keys. Keep the biggest so far in a loop.
Test several days, including an empty one. One test can pass by luck.

segments.say: Here is what you used in this boss level.
Keep each record as a tuple in a list, so nothing is lost.
Build totals with get and a default of 0. A set of allowed values rejects anything else.
Replace with a third value, and is digit, check an amount before float converts it.
Max on a dictionary compares the keys. To find the biggest total, keep the biggest so far in a loop.
And test several days, including an empty one. One test can pass by luck.
